title: Can Anyone Help Me Create a Product Bundle in ERPNext?

posts.name: Petergrge
posts.cooked:
Hi Everyone,
I’m trying to create a product bundle in ERPNext.
Example: Laptop + Mouse + Bag sold together as one package.

I’m not sure about the correct setup

  • How to link the items into one bundle
  • Whether the price is taken from the child items or set manually
  • If I can change bundle contents for a specific order

Can anyone guide me step-by-step?

Thanks in advance!

posts.name: Ahsan Tareen
posts.cooked:

Please consult with documentation;

Hi Everyone,
I’m trying to create a product bundle in ERPNext.
Example: Laptop + Mouse + Bag sold together as one package.

I’m not sure about the correct setup

  • How to link the items into one bundle
  • Whether the price is taken from the child items or set manually
  • If I can change bundle contents for a specific order

Can anyone guide me step-by-step?

Thanks in advance!

Hi @Petergrge

Nice — bundling laptop + mouse + bag is a very common use-case in ERPNext. Below I’ll give a clear, production-safe step-by-step: how to create the bundle, how price is decided, what you can (and shouldn’t) change per order, and a couple of alternative approaches if you need stock for the parent item. I’ll cite the official docs for the key bits. (Product Bundle)

Quick summary

  • Use Product Bundle (a sales-side BOM) and a non-stock Parent Item. Child items are the actual shippable stock items. Frappe Documentation
  • The parent’s selling price is the one fetched for the bundle in sales transactions (you can manage it via Product Bundle master or regular Item Price/Price List rules). Frappe Documentation
  • When you add the parent to a Sales Order/Invoice/Delivery Note, ERPNext explodes the bundle into the Packing List (editable for warehouse/serial/batch); on submit, stock of child items is reduced. (Sales Order)

Step-by-step (Laptop + Mouse + Bag)

  1. Create the child Items (if not already): Laptop, Mouse, Bag. These are stock items with Maintain Stock = Yes.
  2. Create a Parent Item that represents the bundle (e.g., LAPTOP-BUNDLE-01). For this Parent Item set Maintain Stock = No (it’s a virtual item). Docs: Parent must be a non-stock item. Frappe Documentation
  3. Go to: Home → Selling → Items and Pricing → Product Bundle → New.
  • Select the Parent Item.
  • Add child rows: Laptop qty 1, Mouse qty 1, Bag qty 1.
  • Enter the bundle price to be used when selling (the Product Bundle screen allows specifying the parent price). Save. Frappe Documentation
  1. Create a Sales Order or Sales Invoice and add LAPTOP-BUNDLE-01 as the line item.
  • When you save the transaction, ERPNext will populate the Packing List with the 3 child items and their quantities. You’ll be asked to select a Delivery Warehouse and can edit warehouse/serial/batch in Packing List. On submission, ERPNext will deduct stock of the child items from the chosen warehouse(s). (Sales Order)

Pricing: where does the price come from?

  • The Product Bundle master stores a price for the parent which is fetched in sales transactions. Use that field or manage prices through Item Price / Price List if you need price lists or channel-specific prices. (Docs show price for parent is fetched.) Frappe Documentation

Can I change bundle contents for a specific order?

  • You can edit the Packing List generated for the order: change the Warehouse, Serial No, Batch, and quantities for packing/fulfilment. This is the supported place to make fulfillment-level adjustments. Frappe Documentation
  • Replacing a child SKU with a completely different SKU is technically possible (by editing the Packing List rows), but:
    • it breaks the link back to the defined Product Bundle and may confuse reporting/automation,
    • downstream documents (Purchase Order generation, fulfilment logic) might expect the original children,
    • it’s not the “official” way to offer configurable bundles.
  • Recommended approaches if bundle needs to be customized often:
    1. Create multiple Product Bundles (variants) for common configurations (e.g., LAPTOP-BUNDLE-SSD-512, LAPTOP-BUNDLE-SSD-1TB).
    2. Use Sales BOM / Manufacturing + Repack if you want the bundle to be a stock item (see below).
    3. Use a small customization (client script or server hook) to allow selecting options on Sales Order and auto-replace child items in Packing List before save/submit.

There’s been community discussion requesting more advanced configurable bundle behavior — ERPNext’s out-of-the-box support focuses on fixed bundles + editable packing list for fulfilment tweaks. GitHub

If you want the Parent to be a stock item (assemble into stock)

  • If you need to maintain stock for the Parent Item (i.e., you want a stock SKU for the bundle), use a regular BOM and do a Stock Entry → Repack (package components into the finished bundle). The docs recommend BOM + Stock Entry for that workflow. This gives you inventory for the parent and normal manufacturing accounting. Frappe Documentation

Practical tips / Best practices

  • Keep parent as non-stock unless you have to show the bundle as an inventory SKU. Non-stock parent + Product Bundle is simpler for offers and quick selling. Frappe Documentation
  • Manage prices centrally via Price Lists so you can change bundle selling price without editing the bundle master each time.
  • If you plan to let salespeople customize bundles a lot, consider creating a simple UI (client script) that presents common options and builds the correct Product Bundle/packing list programmatically.
  • Test end-to-end: Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice → check Stock Ledger to confirm child stock reduction.
